devanagari:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
iast:
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi ||
meaning: Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not be attached to doing nothing.
reflection: Give today's task your full, honest effort — then let the outcome rest. Results were never fully in your hands.

iast:
mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ |
āgamāpāyino ’nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata ||
meaning: Contact with the world brings heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and they go; they do not last. Bear them patiently.
reflection: This feeling is a visitor, not a resident. Like weather, it arrived and it will pass.

devanagari:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
iast:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya |
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga ucyate ||
meaning: Established in yoga, act without clinging. Stay even-minded in success and failure — this evenness of mind is called yoga.
reflection: Steadiness is not about winning every day. It is about meeting both outcomes with the same quiet heart.

iast:
duḥkheṣv anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ |
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir ucyate ||
meaning: One whose mind is not shaken in sorrow, who does not crave in pleasure, who is free from clinging, fear and anger — that sage is called steady in wisdom.
reflection: Sthira — steady. Not unfeeling, just not swept away. Each calm breath is practice for this.

devanagari:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
iast:
āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭhaṁ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī ||
meaning: As rivers flow into the ocean, which stays full and unmoved, so the one into whom all desires flow without disturbance finds peace — not the one who chases desires.
reflection: Let thoughts and wants flow in like rivers. You can be the ocean: wide enough to hold them, deep enough to stay still.

devanagari:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṁś carati niḥspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||
meaning: One who lets go of cravings and moves through life without grasping, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego — that person reaches peace.
reflection: Peace often arrives not by adding something, but by loosening our grip on something.

devanagari:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
iast:
uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet |
ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||
meaning: Lift yourself up by your own self; do not let yourself sink down. The mind can be your friend, and it can be your enemy.
reflection: Speak to yourself today the way a kind friend would. You are allowed to be on your own side.

devanagari:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
iast:
yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu |
yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā ||
meaning: For one who is balanced in food and rest, balanced in effort at work, and balanced in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the remover of sorrow.
reflection: Small balances matter: a regular bedtime, a pause between tasks, a meal eaten slowly.

devanagari:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
iast:
yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
yogino yata-cittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ ||
meaning: Like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker — that is the image of the settled mind of one absorbed in meditation.
reflection: Picture a small flame, perfectly still. With each out-breath, let the wind around your mind settle a little more.

devanagari:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
iast:
yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram |
tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṁ nayet ||
meaning: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, gently bring it back from there, and rest it again in the Self.
reflection: Wandering is not failure. Noticing and returning — again and again — is the whole practice.

devanagari:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
iast:
asaṁśayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ calam |
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate ||
meaning: Without doubt the mind is restless and hard to hold. But it is steadied by practice and by letting go.
reflection: Even Arjuna found the mind hard to calm. Krishna's answer was gentle: keep practising, and loosen your grip.

devanagari:
ॐ पूर्णमदः पूर्णमिदं पूर्णात्पूर्णमुदच्यते ।
पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते ॥
iast:
oṁ pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṁ pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate |
pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate ||
meaning: That is whole, this is whole. From the whole, the whole arises. Take the whole from the whole, and the whole remains.
reflection: Nothing that happens today can make you less than whole.

devanagari:
असतो मा सद्गमय ।
तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय ।
मृत्योर्मामृतं गमय ॥
iast:
asato mā sad gamaya |
tamaso mā jyotir gamaya |
mṛtyor mā amṛtaṁ gamaya ||
meaning: Lead me from the unreal to the real. Lead me from darkness to light. Lead me from death to immortality.
reflection: A prayer for direction, not perfection: one small step from darkness toward light is enough for today.

devanagari:
उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत ।
क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥
iast:
uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata |
kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṁ pathas tat kavayo vadanti ||
meaning: Arise, awake, and learn from those who know. The wise say the path is as sharp as a razor's edge — hard to walk.
reflection: If things feel hard, it is not because you are doing it wrong. The sages themselves called the path difficult.
